newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain warns against scrapping Zaire aid force.
newsitem.headline: Spain warns against scrapping Zaire aid force.

text.p: Spain on Wednesday sounded a warning that scrapping a multinational force for Zaire would only make a bad situation worse.

The sudden return of half a million refugees to Rwanda from eastern Zaire has prompted a reassessment of the need for international military intervention. Spain, which has been a leading advocate of the force, maintains it is still necessary.
"Just the announcement that the U.N. was going to make a decision helped to put in motion this movement of refugees," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Wednesday.
"In the same manner, just the announcement that the decision may be cancelled could further complicate and aggravate a situation which is already complicated," he said.

Hundreds of thousands of Hutu refugees fled back into Rwanda last weekend to escape fighting between Zairean rebels, supported by Rwanda, and soldiers from Rwanda's Hutu-dominated ex-army and militias, who organised the 1994 Rwandan genocide of minority Tutsis.
Aid workers have estimated another 700,000 displaced Hutus remain in eastern Zaire.
Thousands more refugees, tracked by U.S. satellites, trekked towards Rwanda on Wednesday. A second mass exodus would further weaken the case for a U.N. intervention force.
Spanish Defence Minister Eduardo Serra said the planned 10,000-strong force could probably be scaled back to 1,000 in light of the new developments.

Serra reaffirmed Spain's commitment to send troops but said his government could not make the decision alone. "The Spanish government is absolutely decided on going," he said in a radio interview on Wednesday. "(The government) is doing its best to put an end to this situation."
He said said Spain would be ready to send troops in 10 days.
